groups.text: It is currently 19 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

OpenAI has launched its new GPT-6 Astra model, but users face significantly tighter usage limits than they did with the previous GPT-5.6 Sol. The standard version of Astra offers roughly half as many messages per five-hour window compared to Sol across all plans. Currently, the model is available for those on Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium plans through ChatGPT Work and Codex, with Plus and Business users expected to gain access in the coming days. For those seeking more power, OpenAI also released GPT-6 Astra Pro. Access to this version depends heavily on the subscription tier. The two-hundred-dollar Pro plan allows for 200 messages per week, while the one-hundred-dollar Pro and Business Premium plans are limited to 50. Those on Business Standard plans have the tightest restrictions, receiving only 15 messages per month. The model is also accessible via Microsoft Azure, AWS Bedrock, and the OpenAI API.

Russian attacks killed at least seven people and injured 51 others across Ukraine over the past day. The violence comes as Moscow rejects a ceasefire, despite reports that Ukraine ordered its troops to pause hostilities for four days. This pause was intended to precede visits by U.S. envoys to Kyiv and Moscow in an effort to revive peace talks. Overnight, Russia launched ballistic missiles and 167 drones against 23 locations, though Ukrainian air defenses shot down or suppressed 128 of those drones. The heaviest toll occurred in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, where five people were killed and six others injured across four districts. In Kherson Oblast, two more people died and 27 were injured. Drone attacks in Mykolaiv Oblast injured three people, including a 17-year-old girl, and damaged a shopping mall, a warehouse, transport infrastructure, and several vehicles.

Enterprises are rapidly adopting cloud services, but many now struggle to identify and manage the security risks tied to those applications. This gap in oversight has left most organizations ill-equipped to contain critical security incidents, according to a recent report on incident response. The vulnerability is further complicated by agentic AI, which introduces a new insider threat model for organizations to navigate. These systemic weaknesses are evident in concrete failures, such as the Wi-Fi hack that disrupted Delta flights earlier this year. To address these gaps, Dark Reading is hosting a full-day virtual event focused on securing cloud assets in the age of AI. The session aims to provide enterprises with the tools and best practices needed to maintain a comprehensive view of their multi-cloud infrastructure. By focusing on these insights, companies hope to get ahead of attackers before another critical breach occurs.

Soot pollution from cars, factories, and coal plants is now linked to the collapse of glaciers in the Himalayas. This dark layer of residue weakens the albedo effect, meaning the ice absorbs more solar heat instead of reflecting it back into space. Modeling from the Chinese Academy of Sciences estimates that black carbon from South Asia caused up to one-third of total glacial mass loss between 2007 and 2016. The urgency grew after a disaster in Nepal's valleys at the end of August left thousands missing. Turning to sports, Saturday brings two major matchups for the twenty-sixth round of the Brasileirão. São Paulo faces Atlético-MG at six-thirty p.m. at Morumbis. Later, at nine p.m., Fluminense and Vasco meet at the Maracanã in Rio de Janeiro. Both games will be available on Premiere, with the Fluminense and Vasco clash also airing on sportv.

Organizations are currently scrambling to balance the unprecedented power of AI tools against the security risks they introduce to enterprise operations. This tension is highlighted by a new insider threat model created by agentic AI, which presents fresh challenges for organizational safety. While companies seek to implement proper guardrails for governance and identity, many remain ill-equipped to handle crises; a recent report found that nearly every organization faced a critical security incident last year, yet most could not contain them. These vulnerabilities extend into public infrastructure, as seen in the August disruption of Delta flights caused by a Wi-Fi hack. To address these gaps, industry experts are now focusing on building secure AI strategies and protecting cloud assets. This shift comes as enterprises struggle to keep pace with the breakneck speed of AI adoption while managing newly discovered vulnerabilities and emerging cyber threats.

The shipping industry is moving toward decarbonization with the first ethanol-capable engine from Everllence passing R&D testing in Korea. This tri-fuel G80 engine can run on fuel oil, methanol, or ethanol and is destined for a Very Large Ore Carrier ordered by Shandong Shipping for charter to the Brazilian operator Vale. Delivery is expected in early 2027 as part of a strategy to reduce emissions across maritime logistics. Meanwhile, China plans to launch the Xuntian space telescope next year to accompany the Tiangong space station. The fifteen-ton instrument will act as a "minilua," flying close to the station and docking for maintenance or refueling, which avoids the complex repair missions historically required for tools like NASA's Hubble. In sports, Red Bull Bragantino faces Bahia today at 4 p.m. Brasília time in Bragança for the twenty-sixth round of the Brasileirão, with the match airing live on Premiere.

India has launched a new Seafarer Tracking Module on its e-NAVIK portal to monitor Indian crew members working in high-risk maritime regions. The Directorate General of Maritime Administration says the system is necessary because geopolitical tensions and security threats have increased risks for merchant ships in areas like the Red Sea, the Black Sea, and the Gulf of Aden. While the module is currently in beta, authorities are prioritizing data updates for vessels in five specific zones, including the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, to coordinate faster emergency responses. This push for systemic tracking contrasts with a different debate over accountability in professional fields. In a letter to STAT News, one reader argues that a simple click or signature should not magically transfer legal responsibility from an AI developer or platform to a physician when using artificial intelligence in medicine.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with rain chances up to 83 percent and temperatures between 17 and 20 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
Mail worth checking: Amazon says your silicone brushes are out for delivery today. Also, the Bundesagentur für Arbeit has new messages waiting for you in their portal.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
